key_insight: ReTrace turns a written Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow. Code selects the next step instead of repeatedly asking an LLM to plan.
problem_solved: LLM agents repeatedly executing the same business procedure still use an LLM to choose each step, adding latency and cost even when the underlying process stays the same.
method: Start with a natural-language SOP and a few logged executions by a tool-using agent.
Distill these inputs into a reusable workflow for processing new inputs.
Use code to select subsequent steps, removing LLM-based step selection during workflow execution.
impact: For practitioners automating repetitive business processes, ReTrace offers a way to reduce reliance on repeated LLM planning and potentially lower latency and cost. The provided abstract is truncated and includes no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Transformation diagram: written SOP + logged agent runs → ReTrace → reusable workflow.
Side-by-side execution paths: repeated LLM planning versus code-controlled step selection.
Workflow diagram showing tool calls connected by code-controlled branches.
Latency and cost icons highlighting the overhead targeted by removing repeated planning calls.
paper_title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
paper_authors: Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya, Rohith Nama, Arushi Gupta
